semantics.note: The normalization preserves permission, monthly value, and the person concerned.

contract.note: Permission and retail-equivalent valuation are reasonable readings. Requiring May specifically imposes a period the June statement does not supply. The packet nevertheless lacks allowance evidence for either period.

evidence.note: A dated secondary account of April token consumption. It establishes neither a monthly allowance nor the valuation needed to test the amount.

reviews.rationale: Reported token consumption does not establish permission for the claimed monthly dollar amount. Neither supporting allowance records nor an enforced lower limit appear in the packet.

attribution.note: The categorical denial and causal explanation are Zitron's own assertions.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the absence claim and the proposed chain from pro-AI bias to narrative adoption and stock movements.

contract.note: An operational replacement for the Salesforce functions a company uses is an ordinary reading of building its own Salesforce. Requiring a complete reproduction of the vendor's suite would be unduly restrictive.

evidence.note: Klarna's CEO describes an internal stack and deployed interfaces replacing its Salesforce use. This company disclosure, reported by TechCrunch, challenges the categorical denial; it is not independent verification or evidence of widespread adoption.

Reuters links stock movements to AI-disruption expectations and announcements. This supports the market-effects component, but concrete developments weaken the surrounding denial of any factual basis and do not establish pro-AI bias.

reviews.rationale: Klarna's reported functional replacement contradicts the categorical absence claim. Reuters supports the narrower assertion that AI narratives and expectations moved stocks. The proposed bias-based explanation for narrative adoption remains unestablished.

attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses all three financial assertions.

semantics.note: The amounts and year are preserved, but generic cloud-compute spending broadens the source's scope beyond Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and AWS. The contract restores that restriction.

contract.note: Realized calendar-2025 revenue and spending are ordinary readings. Requiring a defined sector denominator and comparable accounting prevents run rates or unrelated expenses from deciding the result.

evidence.note: Reports approximately $13 billion of OpenAI revenue in 2025, citing FT-confirmed figures. This single-company component cannot establish combined revenue; total expenses and R&D are not named-provider compute spending.

The compute estimates total $23.1 billion and warrant consideration. Their accounting and provider coverage are not reconciled to the claimed realized spending, so they do not establish a comparable contradiction.
Describes annualized revenue for a selected 34-company cohort in May 2026. It cannot establish or refute the share of all AI-startup realized revenue in 2025.

reviews.rationale: The supplied items lack Anthropic's comparable annual revenue, a 2025 sector denominator, and reconciled named-provider compute spending. The lower compute estimate and differently scoped 89% statistic expose evidentiary gaps without settling the actual claims.

attribution.note: Zitron adopts the spending figure as a definite future outcome.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm annual spending forecast and historical comparison.

contract.note: Testing realized 2026 expenditure and using the adjacent 2003–2017 comparison period are fair. Company coverage, expenditure basis, and rounding remain unspecified and must be fixed before final grading.

evidence.note: Goldman Sachs supplies a model-based aggregate AI-infrastructure estimate. It explains the figure's origin but establishes neither realized spending by a defined big-tech cohort nor the historical ratio.

reviews.rationale: Calendar 2026 had not ended by the evaluation date, and no qualifying early-resolution event is documented. An analyst model cannot establish the forecast's outcome; the spending scope and Amazon baseline also remain unreconciled.
